== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-13-threshold|The Dreadgods are a group of four massive, highly intelligent, and destructive entities that serve as a fundamental corruption of the natural order on [[Cradle]]. Driven by an inherent [[hunger]], these monsters are capable of consuming entire mountains and devastating landscapes simply through their presence or movement. They are characterized by a shared [[hunger aspects|hunger aspect]] in their [[madra]] and are considered nearly impossible to kill; if one is slain, the others are drawn to the location and grow stronger, eventually allowing the fallen entity to be reborn. The four known Dreadgods include the [[Bleeding Phoenix]], the [[Wandering Titan]], the [[Weeping Dragon]], and the [[Silent King]], with a fifth entity known as [[Subject One]] or the father of the Dreadgods serving as their progenitor. These beings are deeply connected to the world's power structure, as their existence is tied to the presence of the [[Monarchs]]. While the most powerful individuals in the world, such as [[Monarchs]], can fight them to a stalemate, they cannot defeat them alone. The Dreadgods are also associated with various cults—such as the [[Abyssal Palace]] and [[Redmoon Hall]]—and creatures like [[Blood Shadows]] and [[dreadbeasts]], which are believed to be lesser versions or failures of the Dreadgods. Historically, these entities have sought a specific location known as [[labyrinth|the labyrinth]], which is rumored to be their birthplace and a primary target for their [[hunger]].}}

== Reaper ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-10-reaper|The five Dreadgods, which [[Eithan]] theorizes are successful versions of [[dreadbeasts]], were born within a maze located somewhere in the region. These entities appear as a dragon accompanied by clouds, a tiger with a halo, a shelled warrior, and a bird, and they are currently stronger than ever. While [[Monarchs]] sustain them and maintain an equilibrium to prevent them from growing too powerful, no individual [[Monarch]] can defeat a [[Dreadgod]]. Although they have been driven off for the moment, their presence has carved ravines into the territory around [[Refuge]] and they remain potential future opponents within [[labyrinth|the labyrinth]]. [[Reigan Shen]] expressed a desire to call them together to destroy them, though he also sought to bring the creatures under control. Ultimately, the Dreadgods are anchored to life by a specific element that would make them mortal if removed, and a method to kill them exists inside [[labyrinth|the labyrinth]].}}

== Dreadgod ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-11-dreadgod|Awakened during an apocalyptic battle, the Dreadgods are ancient entities that have existed for thousands of years and are considered nearly impossible to kill. Their existence is a consequence of [[Monarchs]] upsetting a balance on [[Cradle]], serving as the price paid for those [[Monarchs]] to remain on the world. Because all four are currently awake, they represent a looming threat that is actively pursuing [[Lindon]] and [[Yerin]]. While the [[Beast King]] battles them and [[Redmoon]] has sought to borrow their power, [[Lindon]] intends to research these beings with the ultimate goal of killing them. However, destroying a [[Dreadgod]] causes the others to grow stronger and draw together until the fallen entity is eventually reborn.}}

== Waybound ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-12-waybound|The Dreadgods are intelligent, clever beings fundamentally designed to devour the world, though they are not complete monsters like the [[Monarchs]]. While they have historically been able to kill [[Monarchs]], they are so heavy that they must use specific tricks to transport themselves. During their rampage, the two remaining Dreadgods clash in the sky and destroy [[Reigan Shen]]'s continent, moving faster than ever due to being empowered. Although [[Malice]] allowed them to exist and they loom large in various futures, [[Lindon]] eventually kills them, an act that puts him on a timer and results in him losing consciousness. It is possible that these entities may ultimately be sealed within a [[labyrinth]].}}

<li>{{spoiler|book=cradle-12-waybound|The [[Dreadgods]] loom large in the futures [[Malice]] glimpses.<ref name="cradle-12-waybound-c26">''Waybound'', chapter 26</ref>}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=cradle-12-waybound|[[Monarchs]] can go toe-to-toe with [[Dreadgods]].<ref name="cradle-12-waybound-c27">''Waybound'', chapter 27</ref>}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=cradle-12-waybound|[[Malice]] allowed the [[Dreadgods]] to exist.<ref name="cradle-12-waybound-c28">''Waybound'', chapter 28</ref>}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=cradle-12-waybound|The [[Dreadgods]] are closing in on [[Lindon]].<ref name="cradle-12-waybound-c29">''Waybound'', chapter 29</ref>}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=cradle-12-waybound|The [[Dreadgods]] are destroying [[Reigan Shen]]'s continent.<ref name="cradle-12-waybound-c30">''Waybound'', chapter 30</ref>}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=cradle-12-waybound|[[Lindon]] lost consciousness while killing the [[Dreadgods]].<ref name="cradle-12-waybound-c33">''Waybound'', chapter 33</ref>}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=cradle-12-waybound|The [[Dreadgods]] might be sealed in a [[labyrinth]].<ref name="cradle-12-waybound-c35">''Waybound'', chapter 35</ref>}}</li>
</ul></div>

== Notable quotes ==
* {{spoiler|book=cradle-08-wintersteel|“I would like to ensure that the Blackflame Empire is evacuated before the danger of the Dreadgods.”<ref name="cradle-08-wintersteel-c11" />}}
* {{spoiler|book=cradle-10-reaper|“The maze beneath us is the birthplace of the Dreadgods,” Elder Whisper went on,<ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c2" />}}
* {{spoiler|book=cradle-10-reaper|“There’s a way to kill the Dreadgods in there?” Ziel asked.<ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c9" />}}
* {{spoiler|book=cradle-10-reaper|“Disturbing implications, but that was always one of the strongest theories about the origins of the dreadbeasts. That they were the failures, and the successes were the Dreadgods.”<ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c13" />}}
* {{spoiler|book=cradle-11-dreadgod|“I want her to help us fight the Dreadgods.”<ref name="cradle-11-dreadgod-c12" />}}
